advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit an explicit `::notice::`/`::warning::` when `HEAD^` is still unresolvable or diff-cover exits non-zero, so a missing diff-coverage report is distinguishable from a clean one.
evidence: The parameterless `git fetch --deepen=1` here (unlike a fetch with an explicit remote+refspec) may not materialize the parent object on a detached patchset checkout; combined with the trailing `|| true` a missing report emits no notice, unlike the two explicit `::notice::` skip messages guarding the empty-refspec and missing-coverage.xml cases (lines 739, 743).
advisory.finding: The diff-coverage report chain is fully best-effort: `git fetch --deepen=1 || true` followed by `diff-cover ... || true` means that if HEAD^ is still unresolvable after the deepen (e.g. the Gerrit patchset checkout has no parent object and the parameterless `git fetch --deepen=1` cannot fetch it because no remote/refspec is supplied), diff-cover errors are swallowed and the step exits 0 having produced NO report — indistinguishable to the author (the intended consumer) from 'checked and 100% covered'. Because the step is explicitly report-only/non-gating this does not affect any merge verdict, but the intended pre-merge author signal can silently vanish with no diagnostic.
scenarios: Gerrit patchset checkout whose parent commit object was never fetched and `git fetch --deepen=1` cannot resolve it without a remote/refspec — diff-cover fails, `|| true` swallows it, step is green with an empty step summary.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend test_diff_coverage_step_present_... to assert the Gerrit-lane skip guard (`GERRIT_REFSPEC` empty => exit 0), the coverage.xml-absence guard, and `--compare-branch='HEAD^'` in the step's run block.
evidence: Added run: lines in _build-and-test.yml: `if [ -z "$GERRIT_REFSPEC" ]; then` ... `exit 0` and `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch='HEAD^' --fail-under=0`
Commit message: 'Gated to the Gerrit lane (skips when GERRIT_REFSPEC is empty) and compares against the patchset parent (HEAD^)'

tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:243-260 — run_code assertions cover only `--format markdown:`, absence of `--markdown-report`, `--fail-under=0`, and the pinned install regex; no assertion references `GERRIT_REFSPEC`, `-z`, `coverage.xml` guard, or `--compare-branch='HEAD^'`.
ABSENCE: no test in the file asserts the Gerrit-refspec skip guard or the HEAD^ compare-branch, both of which are ADDED (`+`) lines under review.
advisory.finding: The new test asserts the diff-coverage step's cell-gating, format flag, fail-under, and version pin, but does NOT assert the step's newly-added Gerrit-lane skip guard (`if [ -z "$GERRIT_REFSPEC" ]; then ... exit 0`), the coverage.xml-absence guard, or the `--compare-branch='HEAD^'` parent comparison — the commit's central behaviors. A refactor that drops the `-z "$GERRIT_REFSPEC"` guard (so the report-only step runs on the post-merge branch lane the commit says it must SKIP) or changes `--compare-branch='HEAD^'` to `HEAD` leaves the test green.
scenarios: A future edit removes the `[ -z "$GERRIT_REFSPEC" ]` skip and the step runs on the post-merge branch lane where there is no reliable base — the parity suite stays green.
The compare base is changed from `HEAD^` to `HEAD`, silently reporting zero changed lines — undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add assertions on run_code: e.g. `assert 'if [ -z "$GERRIT_REFSPEC" ]' in run_code`, `assert "--compare-branch='HEAD^'" in run_code`, and `assert 'coverage.xml' in run_code` (absence guard), plus assert the step env routes `GERRIT_REFSPEC: ${{ inputs.gerrit-refspec }}` rather than interpolating directly.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain diff-cover's transitive deps (e.g. `uv pip install --constraint` / a lock or hash-pinned requirements file) so the install is actually reproducible, or correct the comment to reflect that only the top-level version is pinned.
evidence: comment claims: "its resolved version and transitive deps cannot float on every run (supply-chain hygiene, epic soupy-bilineate-whiteeye S2 precedent)"

A single `==` on the top-level package does not pin diff-cover's transitive dependency tree (e.g. pluggy, jinja2, chardet, pygments) — pip/uv still resolve those to latest compatible unless a constraints/lock file is supplied.
No `--require-hashes` / `--hash=` present; version pin alone does not verify artifact integrity against tampering on the index or mirror.
advisory.finding: The ad-hoc `uv pip install 'diff-cover==10.5.1'` pins only the top-level package; its transitive dependencies are unconstrained and will re-resolve to latest-compatible versions on every CI run, contradicting the step's own comment claiming 'its resolved version and transitive deps cannot float on every run'.
merged_from: The pinned diff-cover install uses no hash verification, so the fetched artifact is not integrity-checked against a known digest.
scenarios: A transitive dep of diff-cover publishes a new release between CI runs and alters report output or install behavior.
A compromised transitive dep is pulled in at install time with no hash/version guard.
